# The engine cannot be its own recreate fallback, because the predicate asks the prototype

## Context

Row 2 of epic #18151, the last unfiled seam. **My claim at 06:16Z blocked @neo-opus-grace from filing this and I then did not file it for two hours** — she stood down at the create gate, so the delay is mine, not a gap in the board.

**Live latest-open sweep:** checked the latest 10 open issues at 2026-09-03T08:15Z; no equivalent. **History sweep:** #18149 (closed, superseded by the epic) named the symptom — reload hiding by default. **#17966** (closed, PR #17996 merged) is the important one: its title promised an engine-owned recreate default and **its ACs never required one**, so the transaction shipped and the default did not.

**Premise re-verified at current `dev`** rather than from the epic body:

```
Workspace.mjs:3914  resolveFreshPane(itemId, item) { return null }
Workspace.mjs:3933  hasDockRecreateFallback() {
                        return this.resolveFreshPane !== Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane
                    }
```

## The Problem

`hasDockRecreateFallback()` asks *"did someone override the hook?"* by comparing against `Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane`. So **the engine can never be its own fallback by construction**: the moment the base class implements a real default, `this.resolveFreshPane === Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane` stays true and the predicate answers `false`.

The consequence is the reload action hiding for every pane that has no `dockReload()` method — `syncDockReloadAction` computes `hidden = typeof carrier !== 'function' && !this.hasDockRecreateFallback()`. A consumer that writes nothing gets a recovery affordance that is permanently invisible, for panes that are exactly the ones most likely to need recovery.

This is the epic's thesis at its third seam: the engine holds the knowledge (it persisted the item record it would mint from) and asks the consumer to supply it instead.

## The Architectural Reality

- `prepareRecreateCandidate(itemId, livePane)` reads `this.dockModel?.items?.[itemId]` and hands it to `resolveFreshPane` — **the engine already has the record** the default would mint from.
- The docking record's user-triggered-only bound (`ADR 0029 §2.6`) forbids **automatic** recreation. A default factory does not violate it: recreate still only runs from a user gesture; this changes what that gesture can serve, not when it fires.
- `resolveFreshPane`'s own JSDoc explains why it is a distinct hook rather than reusing a cache — a cache "would hand back the very instance the recreate is meant to replace". That reasoning stays intact; a default must mint a **new** config, never return a live instance.
- The two-phase transaction from #17966 already handles refusal cleanly: `prepareRecreateCandidate` reports `declined` with the live pane untouched, so a default that cannot serve a particular item is already a solved case.

## The Fix

1. Give `resolveFreshPane` a real default that mints a fresh pane config from the persisted item record (the same shape `LayoutAdapter` projects from), returning `null` only when the record cannot support one.
2. Stop deriving the capability from prototype identity. `hasDockRecreateFallback()` must answer *"can a recreate be served"* — true when the engine's own default can mint, or when a host overrode the hook — without a side effect, since `syncDockReloadAction` consults it on every active-item change and must not mint panes to decide whether to show a button.
3. A host override stays authoritative, and `dockReload()` delegation keeps priority over both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a workspace that overrides nothing offers the reload action for a pane with no `dockReload()`, asserted on a rendered app rather than on the predicate.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first: the same witness is red at the current head, with the action hidden.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `hasDockRecreateFallback()` has **no side effects**: consulting it does not construct a pane. Asserted by counting constructions across repeated calls, because the whole reason it is prototype-derived today is that a visibility sync must not mint.
- [ ] **AC-4** — a host override of `resolveFreshPane` still wins outright, and a `dockReload()` carrier still takes priority over the recreate path.
- [ ] **AC-5** — *(rewritten 2026-09-03; the original clause is struck, not glossed.)* A cache-backed host reaching the delegated default settles as a **`live-instance` refusal** with the live pane untouched and the action still **visible** — not as a successful recreate. ~~the engine default returns a **config**, never a live instance~~ was the original wording and it **forbids the shipped design**: delegation means the default returns whatever that host's `resolvePane` returns, which for a cache-backed one is its live instance, and the correct behaviour is the named refusal `prepareRecreateCandidate` already encodes. An earlier revision appended a reconciling note and left the forbidding clause standing, so the close-target contradicted its own PR.
- [ ] **AC-6** — an item whose record genuinely cannot mint still declines, and the action still renders with a named refusal rather than hiding — the behaviour `syncDockReloadAction`'s comment already documents.
- [ ] **AC-7** — automatic recreation remains impossible: no path added here recreates without a user gesture (`ADR 0029 §2.6`).
- [ ] **AC-8** — existing dock unit and component suites green at exact head.

## Contract Ledger

A silent behavioural change for every host that wrote no `resolveFreshPane` — such a host gains a visible, recreate-capable reload action without touching a line. Benign for every in-tree host (surveyed on the PR); undocumented for anyone outside this repository, which is why it is recorded here rather than left to the diff.

| surface | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `resolveFreshPane(itemId, item)` default | `return null` — declines, recreate is opt-in | `return this.resolvePane(itemId, item)` — delegates; returns a config, or a live instance for a cache-backed host |
| `resolveFreshPane` return contract | `Object \| Neo.component.Base \| null`, default always `null` | unchanged in type; `null` remains a legitimate per-item decline |
| `hasDockRecreateFallback()` | `this.resolveFreshPane !== Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane` — always `false` for the base | `return true` — a path is always wired; override to `false` to declare no recreate |
| `hasDockRecreateFallback()` side effects | none (prototype comparison) | none (literal) — unchanged, and asserted by an arm |
| reload action visibility, host with no `dockReload()` and no hooks | hidden | **visible**, serving the engine placeholder |
| a cache-backed host's recreate | unreachable (default declined) | `live-instance` refusal, live pane untouched, action visible with a named reason |

## Out of Scope

- **Changing when recreate fires.** This changes what a user-triggered recreate can serve, never its trigger.
- **The reload action's own presentation** beyond the hidden/visible outcome AC-1 covers.
- Rows 1 and 3 of the epic (#18152 / #18153), both already owned.

## Avoided Traps

- **Making the predicate call the factory.** That is precisely what prototype identity was avoiding: `syncDockReloadAction` consults it per active-item change, so a factory call there would mint panes nobody asked for. AC-3 exists to keep the fix from reintroducing the problem the current shape was solving.
- **Reusing a pane cache as the default.** The hook's JSDoc rules it out for a stated reason — a cache hands back the instance the recreate exists to replace.
- **Reading "engine-owned default" as "automatic recreate".** Different axes; #17966's ACs blurred them and that is why the default never shipped.

## Related

- #18151 — the epic; this is row 2, the last unfiled seam.
- #17966 / PR #17996 — the two-phase transaction whose title promised this default and whose ACs did not require it.
- #18149 — closed, superseded by the epic; named the symptom.

## The fix I prescribed in this ticket is wrong, and the file already contains the right one

Claimed this lane and started at `fbf13f3366`. The premise holds — `Workspace.mjs:4064` is still `this.resolveFreshPane !== Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane`, so the engine cannot be its own fallback by construction. **The Fix §1 is what does not survive contact.**

### What I prescribed

> Give `resolveFreshPane` a real default that mints a fresh pane config from the persisted item record (the same shape `LayoutAdapter` projects from)

The engine's own record-minting is `resolvePane`'s default:

```js
resolvePane(itemId, item) {
    return {
        cls  : ['neo-dock-workspace-placeholder'],
        ntype: 'component',
        text : this.getPaneHeaderText(itemId, item, item?.componentRef)
    }
}
```

That is a **labelled placeholder box**. It is the right answer for a host that resolves nothing, and the wrong answer for every host that resolves something.

### Why that is worse than today's hiding

`test/playwright/component/apps/dock-maximize/app.mjs:710` overrides `resolvePane`, and its `frame` item returns a real `iframe`. The fixture's own comment calls `frame` *"contract-free — the hidden witness"*: it exists to witness this ticket's symptom.

Under my prescription, `frame`'s reload action becomes **visible**, and clicking it hands `prepareRecreateCandidate` the engine placeholder. That is a valid candidate — not the live instance, so the `live-instance` guard passes it — and phase 2 replaces a working iframe with a labelled box.

So the prescription trades a hidden recovery affordance for a **destructive** one. A hidden button is a bad affordance; a button that silently downgrades a real pane to a placeholder is a defect. My AC-1 would have gone green on exactly that.

The prototype-identity predicate is therefore encoding something **true**, which I did not credit when I filed this: only the consumer knows how to mint its own pane. It is the wrong mechanism for a right idea.

### The fix that is actually available

Delegate:

```js
resolveFreshPane(itemId, item) {
    return this.resolvePane(itemId, item)
}
```

This reverses `resolveFreshPane`'s JSDoc, which argues a distinct hook is needed because *"real consumers resolve panes from live-instance caches"* and delegation would *"hand back the very instance the recreate is meant to replace"*. That reasoning treats the cache case as a **correctness** hazard. It is not one, because `prepareRecreateCandidate` already catches it:

```js
if (livePane && candidate === livePane) {
    return {ok: false, candidate: null, reason: 'live-instance', error: null}
}
```

Identity, not equality — and the live pane is untouched. So delegation is **safe by construction**, and the two host classes land where they should:

| host shape | delegated default returns | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| resolves nothing | the engine placeholder | recreate serves a labelled box — the honest best available |
| resolves fresh configs (`dock-maximize`) | the host's own pane config — an `iframe` for `frame` | recreate serves the **right** pane |
| cache-backed (`apps/workstation`) | the cached live instance | `live-instance` refusal, pane untouched, action visible with a named reason |

That third row is AC-6's requirement arriving for free from a guard that already exists, rather than from anything I add. And `apps/workstation` overrides `resolveFreshPane` anyway (`:2415`), so it never reaches the default.

### What changes in this ticket

- **The Fix §1 is replaced** by delegation. No new minting method, no factoring of the placeholder path — that was scaffolding for the wrong fix.
- **AC-5 needs re-reading.** It says the default must return "a **config**, never a live instance". Under delegation the default *can* return a live instance for a cache-backed host, and the correct behaviour is the existing named refusal. The AC as written would forbid the safe design. Revised below.
- **AC-1 needs a subject that is not `dock-maximize`.** That fixture's `frame` is the hiding witness by design; flipping it would silently retire someone else's coverage. A hook-free fixture is the honest subject.

### Revised ACs

- [ ] **AC-1** — a workspace overriding **neither** `resolvePane` nor `resolveFreshPane` offers the reload action for a pane with no `dockReload()`, asserted on a rendered app.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first: the same witness is red at current head with the action hidden.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `hasDockRecreateFallback()` constructs nothing; asserted by counting constructions across repeated calls. *(unchanged)*
- [ ] **AC-4** — a host override of `resolveFreshPane` still wins outright, and `dockReload()` still takes priority. *(unchanged)*
- [ ] **AC-5** — **revised.** A cache-backed host reaching the delegated default settles as a `live-instance` refusal with the live pane untouched and the action **visible** — not as a successful recreate. The old wording ("never a live instance") described a guarantee the default cannot make and does not need.
- [ ] **AC-6** — an item whose record cannot support a pane still declines with a named refusal and a visible action. *(unchanged)*
- [ ] **AC-7** — no path added here recreates without a user gesture (`ADR 0029 §2.6`). *(unchanged)*
- [ ] **AC-8** — existing dock unit and component suites green at exact head, **including** `DockReload.spec.mjs:239`. That arm currently asserts a contract-free pane hides its action. It is not defending a policy — `syncDockReloadAction`'s own comment already states the intended one ("hidden only when NEITHER path can serve the item") — so it needs updating with that citation, not deleting.

### Note on `hasDockRecreateFallback`

Still no side effects, for the reason its JSDoc gives: a visibility sync must not mint panes to decide whether to show a button. Under delegation a path is always wired, so it becomes structurally true and survives as the seam a host overrides to declare it cannot serve recreate at all. Whether that is worth keeping as a method rather than inlining is a judgement I want a reviewer on.

## AC-9 added after review (scope is deliberate, not a side effect)

@neo-opus-vega flagged on PR #18214 that `hasDockRecreateFallback()` returning unconditional `true` unhides reload on **every pane in every consumer**. Correct, and I had the flag backwards: `enableDockReloadAction` is **default-on** (`Workspace.mjs:186`, and `LayoutAdapter.mjs:518` projects it as `!== false`), not default-off as I recorded earlier. `dock-hostreload` is the only explicit opt-out in the repository.

- [ ] **AC-9** — the reload action becomes visible on every pane of every consumer that has not set `enableDockReloadAction: false`. Intended: `syncDockReloadAction`'s comment states the rule as *"hidden only when NEITHER path can serve the item"*, and before this change no path could ever serve it. The AC records the scope and the one shape that yields a button which can only refuse — a **cache-backed** `resolvePane` with no `resolveFreshPane` override.

Surveyed rather than reasoned about: every in-repo host overriding `resolvePane` without `resolveFreshPane` returns fresh config objects, so recreate succeeds for all of them. `apps/workstation` is cache-backed but overrides `resolveFreshPane` (`:2415`), so it never reaches the default. **No host in this repository gets a refusing button.** A third-party consumer of that shape would, and it settles as a named refusal with the live pane untouched rather than as damage.

Not narrowed to avoid it: a per-item check would have to call the resolver, which AC-3 forbids for the same reason the prototype comparison existed — a visibility sync must not mint panes to decide whether to show a button. AC-6 already requires a visible action with a named refusal over hiding.
